sentences.text: This Claim Petition is filed by the Petitioner against the Respondents under Section 166 of the Motor Vehicles Act seeking Compensation of 15,00,000/ for the injuries sustained in a Road Traffic accident.

2. The substance of averments made in the Petition is as under:
That on 04.08.2020 at about 5.30 p.m, when the Petitioner was riding a two wheeler bearing Reg.No.KA42EB0202 and reached near Kottagarahalli village,
Gejjagaraguppe - Jalamangala road, Madbal Hobli, Magadi Taluk, at that time, SCCH 15 3 MVC No.2702/2020 one Tata Sumo bearing Reg.No.KA18M5916 driven by its driver came in a high speed and in a rash and negligent manner and dashed against the Petitioner's vehicle.
Due to which the Petitioner has sustained grievous injuries to all over the body.

3. Immediately after the accident, the Petitioner was shifted to Ramakrishna hospital, Ramanagara,
wherein he has undergone surgery.

He spent more than Rs.3,00,000/ towards medical,
conveyance, nourishment and other incidental charges.
4. Prior to the date of accident, the Petitioner was hale and healthy and he was working as Coolie and was earning 800/ per day.
The said accident has occurred due to the rash and negligent driving of the offending Tata Sumo bearing Reg.No.KA18M5916 by its driver.
The Respondent No.1 is the owner of the offending vehicle and the Respondent No.2 is the insurer of the offending vehicle and
therefore Respondent SCCH 15 4 MVC No.2702/2020 No.1 and 2 are jointly and severally liable to pay compensation to the Petitioner.
Hence, this Petition.
5. In pursuance of service of Notice to the Respondents, the Respondent No.1 remained absent and he was placed exparte.
The Respondent No.2 had appeared before the Court through its Counsel and filed its Written statement to the main Petition.

The Respondent No.2 filed its Written statement inter alia denied the age, avocation and income of the Petitioner and also denied the accident caused by the rash and negligent driving of the driver of the offending vehicle.
Further it has denied the injuries sustained by the Petitioner in the accident and the expenses incurred for the medical treatment.

Further contended that, the Petitioner was riding his two wheeler bearing Reg.No.KA42EB0202 on the road in a zigzag speedy manner on the center of the road and dashed against the Tata Sumo bearing Reg.No.KA18M5916.
The Petitioner was solely SCCH 15 5 MVC No.2702/2020 responsible for the accident.
Hence, it is not liable to pay compensation to the Petitioner.
On these grounds, Respondent No.2 has prayed to dismiss the petition against it.

6. On the rival Pleadings, this Court has framed the following Issues:
ISSUES

sentences.text: 2 1. Whether the Petitioner proves that he had sustained grievous injuries in the Road Traffic Accident that occurred on 04.08.2020 at about 05.30 p.m., near Kottagarahalli village, Gejjagaraguppe - Jalmangala road, Madbal hobli, Magadi taluk, due to the rash and negligent driving of the driver of Tata Sumo bearing Reg.No.KA18M5916?
2. Whether the Petitioner is entitled for the compensation as prayed for?
If yes, what is the quantum and who is liable to pay ?
3. What Order or Award?
In order to prove the case of the Petitioner, the Petitioner got examined himself as P.W.1 and got marked 11 documents at Ex.P.1 to Ex.P11.
Further, he examined one witness as PW.2 and got marked 2 documents at Ex.12 and 13 and closed his side evidence.
On the other hand, Respondent No.2 did not choose to lead any evidence.

8. Having heard the arguments and upon perusal of the written Arguments filed by the Petitioner and depositions, documents exhibited and materials available on record, my answer to the above Issues are as under:
 Issue No.1 : In the Affirmative.
 Issue No.2 : Partly in the Affirmative  Issue No.3 : As per the Final Order,
 for the following :
 REASONS 9. Issue No.1 : It is the case of the Petitioner that, he had sustained grievous injuries in the Road Traffic Accident that occurred due to the rash and negligent driving of the SCCH 15 7 MVC No.2702/2020 offending Tata Sumo bearing Reg.No.KA18M 5916 by its driver.
10. On the other hand, the Respondent No.2 has denied the accident occurred by the rash and negligent driving of the offending Tata Sumo bearing Reg.No.KA18M 5916 by its driver.

11. In order to prove the case of the Petitioner, the Petitioner got examined himself as P.W.1 and got marked 11 documents at Ex.P1 to Ex.P11 and he has reiterated the Petition averments in his Chiefaffidavit.
Ex.P1 to Ex.P6 are the True copies of FIR, Complaint, Spot mahazar, IMV report, Wound Certificate and Charge sheet.
Ex.P7 & 8 are the Discharge summaries.
Ex.P9 is the Medical bills.

Further, the Petitioner has examined Doctor by name Dr. Nagaraj B.N as P.W.2 and got marked 2 documents at Ex.P.12 and 13.
16.

sentences.text: Accordingly, I answer Issue No.1 in the 'Affirmative'.

SCCH 15 11 MVC No.2702/2020 17. Issue No.2: As the Petitioner has proved that the accident has occurred due to the rash and negligent driving of the offending Tata Sumo vehicle by its driver, the Petitioner is entitled for compensation.
18. In the Petition, the Petitioner has shown his age as 45 years.
In the Wound certificate i.e., Ex.P 5, the age of the Petitioner was shown as 46 years.
The Petitioner has not produced any other documents for his age proof.
Hence, in the absence of any other documents, the age mentioned in the Ex.P5 i.e., Wound Certificate i.e., 46 years to be taken for consideration.
19. Further, the Petitioner has averred that, he was working as Coolie and was earning 800/ per day.
But, he has not produced any document in this regard.
Therefore, in the absence of income proof, the notional income to be taken at Rs.14,500/ per month for the purpose of assessment of compensation.
With this background, the quantum of compensation to which the Petitioner is entitled may be adjudicated.

For the sake of convenience, discussion may be had under following heads :
I. COMPENSATION TOWARDS PAIN, SHOCK AND SUFFERING :
21.

The Wound Certificate i.e., Ex.P5 issued by the Medical Officer of the Ramakrishna hospital,
Ramanagara, shows that in the said accident the Petitioner has sustained following injuries i.e.,
1) Comminuted fracture of mid shaft of right femur.
2) Deglove injury of right knee 3) CLW over right popliteal fossa (6X2cm)
4) CLW 8cm over right calf.
As per the opinion of the Doctor, the injuries are grievous in nature.

Having regard to the nature of injuries sustained by the Petitioner, I am of the opinion that,
awarding compensation of 50,000/ under this head would be just and reasonable.

Manjunatha Alias Manja vs Dinesh C.R on 11 January, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/164530572/
5

entities.text: Manjunatha Alias Manja vs Dinesh C.R
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: II. COMPENSATION TOWARDS LOSS OF AMENITIES :
23. Bearing in mind the nature of the injuries sustained by the Petitioner, I am of the opinion that awarding compensation of 30,000/ under this head would be just and reasonable.

III. COMPENSATION TOWARDS LOSS OF INCOME DURING THE LAID-UP PERIOD:
24.

The Petitioner deposed in his evidence that he had taken treatment at Ramakrishna hospital,
Ramanagara.

Upon going through Ex.P.7, 8 and 10  Discharge summaries of Mathrushree Orthopaedic and Trauma Centre and Ramakrishna hospital shows that the Petitioner was admitted as an inpatient in the said hospital from 05.04.2021 to SCCH 15 14 MVC No.2702/2020 09.04.2021,
04.08.2020 to 10.08.2020 and 06.10.2022 to 09.10.2022.
Therefore, while calculating the total period of which the Petitioner was admitted as an inpatient, it comes to 20 days.
25. Having regard to the nature of injuries sustained by the Petitioner, I am of the opinion that the laid up period may be considered as three months.

Hence, the Petitioner is entitled for compensation of 43,500/ under this head (@ 14,500/ per month ).
IV.
COMPENSATION TOWARDS ATTENDANT'S CHARGES, EXTRA DIET & NOURISHMENT AND CONVEYANCE :

26. Admittedly, the Petitioner has sustained injuries and during the laid up period, the Petitioner might have engaged an attendant and also he might have spent some amount towards extra diet and nourishment and for his conveyance.

In the facts and circumstances of the case, awarding compensation of 9,000/ (@ 100/ per day) towards SCCH 15 15 MVC No.2702/2020 attendants charges, 9,000/ towards extra diet and nourishment and 9,000/ towards conveyance would be just and reasonable.
In all, the Petitioner is entitled for compensation of 27,000/ under this head.
V.COMPENSATION TOWARDS MEDICAL EXPENCES :
27. The petitioner has stated in his evidence that, he had spent more than Rs.3,00,000/ towards medical and other incidental charges.
In order to prove this fact, he has produced total 93 medical bills and hospital bills total amounting to 3,69,219/ which are marked at Ex.P9 & 11.
I have gone through the medical bills.
The acceptable medical bills comes to Rs.3,14,713/.
Hence, by rounding off the same, the same to be taken at 3,14,800/.
Hence, I am of the opinion that the Petitioner is entitled for 3,14,800/ under this head.
SCCH 15 16 MVC No.2702/2020 VI. COMPENSATION TOWARDS LOSS OF FUTURE EARNINGS / COMPENSATION TOWARDS PERMANENT DISABILITY:
28. The petitioner has stated that due to the injuries sustained by him in the accident, he has suffered permanent disablement and he is not able to do his work as he used to do earlier.
Even in his evidence, P.W.1 has deposed to that effect.

Manjunatha Alias Manja vs Dinesh C.R on 11 January, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/164530572/
6 29.

sentences.text: Further, the Petitioner got examined one witness by name Dr. Nagaraj B.N. as P.W.2 who has deposed regarding the injuries sustained by the Petitioner in a Road Traffic Accident and the treatment taken by him at Ramakrishna hospital.
Further, he assessed the whole body disability at 18%.
PW.2 got marked Clinical Notes and Xray and CT scan films at Ex.P12 and 13.
In the cross examination, he has deposed that, he is not the treated doctor and not prescribed any medicines.
Further he deposed that, fracture of the Petitioner is not united and the implants are in situ.

Having regard to the medical records placed on record, the evidence of SCCH 15 17 MVC No.2702/2020 P.W.2 and the nature of the injuries sustained by the Petitioner, I am of the opinion that considering the disability of the Petitioner with respect to the whole body at 10% would be just and proper.
30. As per Sarla Verma's Case (2009 ACJ 1298 SC), the multiplier applicable to the Petitioner is 13.

With multiplier of 13, income of 14,500/ per month and disability of the Petitioner with respect to his whole body at 10%, the loss of future income comes to 2,26,200/ (14,500/ x 12 =
1,74,000/, 1,74,000/x 13 x 10/100 = 2,26,200/).
Hence, the Petitioner is entitled for compensation of 2,26,200/ under this head.

TOTAL COMPENSATION TO WHICH THE PETITIONER IS ENTITLED:
31.

To sum up, the Petitioner is entitled for compensation under the following heads :
 SCCH 15 18 MVC No.2702/2020 1. Pain, shock & Suffering  50,000 /
2. Loss of amenities  30,000/
3. Loss of income during the laid  43,500/
 up period 4. Attendant's charges, Extra diet,  27,000/
 and conveyance 5.

Medical expenses 3,14,800/
6. Loss of Future Income 2,26,200/
 Total 6,91,500/
32.
Thus, totally the Petitioner is awarded compensation of 6,91,500/ with costs and simple interest at 6% p.a. from the date of this petition till the date of realization.

33. Regarding Liability: This Court has arrived at the conclusion that the accident has been occurred by the rash and negligent driving on the part of the driver of the Offending Tata Sumo bearing Manjunatha Alias Manja vs Dinesh C.R on 11 January, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/164530572/
7 Reg.No.KA18M5916.
There is no dispute about the validity of the Policy at the time of the accident.
In this case, the Respondent No.1 is the owner and Respondent SCCH 15 19 MVC No.2702/2020 No.2 is the insurer of the offending vehicle.
Therefore, the Respondent No.1 and 2 are jointly and severally liable to satisfy the award amount.
The Respondent No.2, who is liable to indemnify the Respondent No.1, has to pay the compensation amount to the Petitioner.

Accordingly,
I answer Issue No.2 "Partly in the Affirmative".
34. Issue No.3:

In view of my findings on Issues No. 1 and 2, I proceed to pass the following:
ORDER
The Claim Petition filed by the Petitioner against the Respondents U/S 166 of M.V. Act is hereby allowed in part with costs.
The Petitioner is entitled for  Compensation of 6,91,500/ along with interest at the rate of 6% per annum from the date of the Petition till the date of deposit of Award amount.
SCCH 15 20 MVC No.2702/2020 The Respondent No.1 and 2 are jointly and severally liable to pay the compensation amount to the Petitioner.
The Respondent No.2 being the insurer, is directed to deposit the Award amount and interest within 60 days from the date of the Award.
Out of the compensation amount awarded to the Petitioner, 75% of the award amount with accrued interest shall be released to the Petitioner by way of E payment and after proper identification.
The remaining 25% award amount shall be deposited as F.D. in the name of the Petitioner in any Nationalized or Schedule bank for a period of three years.
The Advocate fee is fixed at 1,000/.
Draw Award accordingly.
